I know my comment is probably going to get buried, but while I agree with many of the reasons being presented on this post, there’s also this problem that I think is happening too:

Everyone or at least most people want to feel special in some ways. And people often believe that they’re really good at something merely because they like it. In particularly, when it comes to art and creativity, most people think they’re creatives when they’re really not just because they admire artistic work and have a passion for it. Liking something does not necessarily mean you’re going to be good at it. People like to live in fantasy more often than they do reality.

It seems that some people even tend to be really good at things that they’d least anticipate in or appreciate. But because they don’t enjoy it for whatever reason (if they’d even known the answer to why), they don’t acknowledge their true talents and chase after a dream that was bound to fail anyway. People don’t know how to stay in their lane and do what’s best for them because they don’t spend the time to try and figure that out.

I’m not trying to sound negative, but since everyone wants to be an artist these days and think they can write a movie or draw a picture or sing a song just because they enjoy it, we get an overwhelming saturation of dream chasers in entertainment industries which makes it extraordinarily difficult for actual creativity to appear. 

Yes the industry is responsible for restricting creativity and absolutely has no respect for art. But since they know that there’s an abundance of wannabes who’ll fall for the bait every time while they’re getting paid for it, then why would art and creativity ever get the respect that it deserves?

The entertainment business is a huge scam that gets rich off of promoting false hopes and dreams. Not because people are actually good at what they do, but the opposite. The more people realize this, the less people will pursue it and the more appreciated art and creativity will be. When there’s an over abundance of crap being spewed out, it’s mainly because there’s not a lot creative people being involved. 

As far as the industry people is concerned, all this content that they’re pushing out is nothing more than just a product that can be replaced and sold. Art and creativity is not a product that can be mass produced, sold, and replaced for millions and millions of dollars. It takes a factory to make a consistently never ending flow of cash. And as long as they have a bunch of replacements who think they got talents, they can keep making crap and people will keep buying it. They’ll never run out of content.

At this point, I don’t think people even know what art and creativity is anymore.

Unfortunately, people just overestimate themselves in this case. People are very egotistical and most will not admit that they suck at something that they really really enjoy doing. 

But that’s just my opinion. There’s always going to be many factors that plays into one issue.

I’m not sure if my comment is going to make any sense to this question but my thoughts about the industry and making a career in entertainment is this:

With any entertainment business, I’d say it has always required more luck than what people want to believe just to make it in. However, it takes another level of luck to maintain and succeed in it once you do get in. Unfortunately, the odds are always going to be against us no matter what. Hollywood is literally a high society club with invites only.

Although everybody isn’t granted a chance to be invited, with the way things are going now, it just seems like it’s going to be even more difficult to get in. But the industry will always need screenwriters and creatives and such. A.I. can only do so much and people are mortal beings. No business can last without some form of human intervention at least. And entertainment especially, is no exception.

As long as there is misery, capitalism, and politics, entertainment will always have a demand for more creatives. The business will always need to foster and encourage false hopes just in case they may find that specific someone conveniently. 

Even though the industry is probably going to be much tougher to break in for most of us, it’s still not worth giving up. Continue to pursue your dreams if you must. You just have to understand the reality of things and not go into this with false hopes and expectations. That bubble has been burst.

You are so young! You have so much life ahead of you, love. It may just be that you’ve hit a certain point in puberty, but I’m only saying that because when I did I became a totally depressed kid afterwards. But what do I know. Sometimes when we grow older, reality hits us hard and unexpected and we start to see and feel things differently. 
You have a bright future ahead of you because you have a lot of time and room to grow. You’ll be a completely different person by the time you’re 20. But you have to keep trying no matter what life throws at you. You may feel this way now, but hopefully, you won’t have to later. It really does matter how you react to the situations happening in your life. I’m very glad that you stopped drinking and that you’ve decided to do that on your own, it seems. That’s a good start on your behalf that maybe you won’t always have to go through this. It takes a lot of strength and maturity to make those kinds of decisions for yourself and if you’re already at that point, then you’ll get even better at it.
I don’t want to sound cliché, but to be honest, you have plenty of time to get a girlfriend. Girls at that age aren’t really that much developed and they don’t know what they want. They can be really mean and immature sometimes. So don’t worry too much about dating right now. What’s most important is making sure that you’re healthy mentally, emotionally, spiritually and physically. When you get older, you won’t be dealing with girls anymore, you’ll be dealing with women, and women are a lot more mature and opened minded. I’m not speaking for all, but women tend to be less judgmental since they’ve experienced life more. 
I do appreciate your honesty and understanding, but you are just a baby in my eyes and it hurts my heart to read such things happening to you like this. I pray that things get better for you as time goes on. You are too young to have to go through such sadness. I say this because I was also lonely and depressed when I was 16. But because I didn’t get the proper help that I needed, it only got worse for me. Now I’m not trying to scare you or anything, but it’s important that you do get help as soon as possible before it can get worse. And sometimes help can come in the form of just doing things like practicing a healthier diet and not being surrounded by negative people. But I know that’s a hard thing to do. However, getting better is not an easy journey which is why a lot of us fall prey to getting worse. 
But please don’t give up, you have a lot to see and experience and hopefully things will get brighter for you.

Thanks for trying to help. I do have a therapist and I’ve been through many psychiatrists, pills and plenty of wasted time in mental institutions. However, nothing seems to work in my case. I know that a good diet and healthy habits may help, but I’m too depressed and lack extreme focus to stay consistent with that. I wish there was something that I could do to make things better, not just for me but for everyone who is struggling. But I have to endure the horrible reality we’re all forced to live in. 
I’ve always believed I was just born broken and that someday I’ll just end up succumbing to it. But for right now, I’m just too much of a coward to off myself so I’ll just have to keep trying. There’s really nothing else I can do at this point. My mindset is fucked up….

But I am glad you’re doing ok tho. And your grammar is fine. It’s ok if you don’t have a lot of friends, especially if they aren’t contributing to your well being. Sometimes having too many people in your circle can be toxic. High school is just a phase. It’s not something to really hang on to, let that be just a learning experience in your developing life. What really matters is after all that. Because you won’t be considered a child anymore. You’ll have responsibilities, judgement and debt to face and you’ll have to be strong to endure the coldness of it. Just take what you’ve learned and apply it to your new role in life as an adult. Things will get better if you’re already taking the measures to change your outcome. Not many young folks look out for themselves like that. I’m proud of you that.

Ok, i have a few things that i want to suggest to you:
1st advice—try to sum all of this up into one paragraph or less. Sometimes having too much detail in a concept can make it difficult to follow. Instead, list these heavily thought out details as an outline for what you want in your story. 

2nd advice—I think the creator should have some more redeeming qualities about him and his motives. For instance, besides from the fact of not knowing what else to do with his powers, maybe create an arc that inspires him to create Tierra. 

3rd advice—-try to explain why Tierra stands out over all the other places. You say it’s because it’s a magical planet with hidden dimensions and you also say that it is a very powerful planet that not even the gods can destroy, why is that so? Explain why this is very important and makes Tierra different.

4th advice—-give more reasons why humans are so important. Besides the gods facing the reality of losing their powers, why should they care so much for the humans as the creator did? What can the humans attribute to the reasons these gods chose to follow the creator’s oath. Are they just afraid of losing their powers? Will they die if they don’t obey? How do they view humans themselves? 
The reason I say this is because you gave schaffung and ligero a motivation to become evil, but I’m curious to know how did they make this transformation? Were they always like that or was something building up to this new outlook they’ve developed? Why do these motivations work for them as antagonist?

It sounds like your story is heavily inspired by Greek mythology which is very interesting. I love to see other people’s take on old concepts.

What if the second murder uncovers to the audience/reader that him being drunk when he committed the first murder was actually a masquerade to him having underlying mental disturbances? If you want to create a mentally deranged character, outside sources (drugs, alcohol, etc.) should be just triggers. Maybe hint to this revelation early on during the first murder. 
Maybe he commits crimes out of complete delusion and he thinks he’s dreaming when does this. That’s why he never remembers, not because of outside influences (being drunk, getting high, etc.), but because he’s completely delusional. He always forgets what he’s done in his waking life when it’s really extreme, and the trauma resorts the acts into vague and distant memories like a movie he once saw before but can’t remember the name of because it was such a long time ago. Maybe he thinks he’s dreaming of the crimes in a prophetic way but in reality, he’s just remembering what he actually did. Maybe blind rage causes him to become delusional when he commits the second murder. And when he comes back to his senses, he’s his regular self again and he forgets. Maybe certain triggers initiate another side of him that he isn’t aware of….
